Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Unity Insurance Group third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Unity Insurance Group's third quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; David Kim, Chief Investment Officer; and Jennifer Hayes, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Unity Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by the strategic impact of our pricing adjustments boosting premium volumes amid market challenges like inflation in repair costs and catastrophe activity, solid net written premiums growth across personal and commercial lines, a prudent asset allocation balancing fixed income stability with equity and alternative upside, improving loss ratios from lower claims frequency and managed severity trends, favorable updates to actuarial assumptions enhancing reserve positions, robust investment income yields from higher reinvestment rates, and clear combined ratio guidance pointing to sustained profitability. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives, including AI-powered pricing tools and telematics expansions.

Michael Chen, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included disciplined pricing actions that propelled premium growth, strong net written premiums expansion by line of business, favorable loss ratio dynamics, actuarial refinements, elevated investment yields, and a resilient combined ratio.

Let me start by diving deep into one of the key drivers behind our top-line performance: the impact of pricing changes on premium volume. This has been a pivotal lever in navigating persistent inflation in auto repair costs, elevated catastrophe activity, and softening competitive pressures in select lines. Overall, our consolidated gross written premiums grew 8.2% year-over-year to $14.7 billion in Q3, marking the 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth on a two-year stacked basis. Pricing discipline contributed approximately 65% of that growth, or 5.3 percentage points, while organic volume expansion and mix shift added the remainder. This reflects our commitment to rate adequacy amid a combined ratio of 92.4%—our best in five years—driven by disciplined underwriting and proactive repricing.

In Personal Lines, which represent 55% of our book, Personal Auto saw average rate increases of 9.2% across renewals, up from 7.8% in Q2, targeting loss trends exacerbated by a 15% YoY rise in severity from higher parts and labor costs, including OEM parts mandates and wage inflation for body shops. This pricing action more than offset a modest 1.8% decline in policies-in-force, resulting in 7.5% premium growth to $4.2 billion. Retention held steady at 87.5%, but we saw some elasticity in price-sensitive markets like California, where new business submissions dipped 4% quarter-over-quarter due to Proposition 103 rate filing scrutiny. Our telematics program, now penetrating 42% of our auto book via the UnityDrive app—similar to Progressive's Snapshot—has enabled 12-15% discounts for safe drivers and supported granular pricing by risk tier.

Homeowners pricing averaged 11.5% increases, fueled by reinsurance cost escalation post-Hurricane Idalia and ongoing wildfire exposure in the West. Premiums here surged 12.1% to $3.1 billion, even as we selectively non-renewed 2.5% of our Florida coastal book to maintain a 15% cap on wind exposure. This mirrors actions by peers like Travelers and Chubb, who've pulled back from high-cat zones. Nationally, we grew policies-in-force by 3.2% through cross-sell initiatives, bundling with our new parametric flood product launched in Q1.

Shifting to Commercial Lines, which drove 42% of our premium growth, we executed 8.7% average rate hikes—flat sequentially but up 200 basis points YoY—amid stabilizing loss costs. Middle-market workers' comp saw the strongest lift at 10.3%, reflecting OSHA-mandated safety upgrades and medical inflation. Overall, premiums expanded 9.8% to $6.9 billion, with flat policy count as we prioritized profitability over share in excess & surplus lines, where we achieved 14.2% rate gains akin to Berkshire Hathaway's National Indemnity approach.

A key technical initiative here has been our AI-powered pricing engine, UnityPrice 2.0, which integrates GLMs with alternative data sources like satellite imagery for property risk and IoT telematics for fleet auto. This has improved rate accuracy by 18%, reducing adverse selection and boosting our earned premium yield by 2.5 points. We've rolled this out to 75% of our commercial book, similar to how Lemonade leverages AI in personal lines but scaled for complex risks.

Regionally, U.S. operations—72% of premiums—benefited from broad-based pricing power, with Southeast rates up 13% due to Hurricane Helene's $5 billion industry loss estimate. Europe, via our Lloyd's syndicate and direct EU platforms, saw more muted 6.1% increases constrained by Solvency II capital charges, but premiums still grew 7.9% in sterling terms, led by UK motor amid rising claims frequency. In Asia-Pacific, our joint venture with Ping An in China delivered 11.2% premium growth on 9% pricing, capitalizing on urbanization-driven commercial demand, though we tempered auto expansion amid EV transition risks.

Strategically, our pricing actions underscore a 'growth through profitability' mantra. We've maintained pricing elasticity below 0.4—meaning a 10% rate hike yields less than 4% volume loss—thanks to superior product innovation and digital distribution, where 68% of new business now flows through our myUnity portal. This positions us favorably versus peers like Allstate, who've faced retention erosion from aggressive hikes. Looking ahead, we expect Q4 pricing to moderate to 7-8% as loss trends peak, with premium growth of 7-9%. Risks include auto frequency rebound from mileage normalization post-COVID and regulatory pushback in California and New York. Mitigants include continued investment in catastrophe modeling with RMS v18.0 and our $250 million cat bond issuance in September, locking in favorable terms at 4.5% all-in cost.

As we dive further into the financials, net written premiums, or NWP, grew 9.2% year-over-year to $4.8 billion. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-cat growth and underscores the strength of our underwriting discipline amid a persistently hardening market. Personal Lines, representing 42% of total NWP, grew 7.8% to $2.0 billion. Homeowners and Other Dwelling led with 12.1% growth, fueled by mid-single-digit rate increases averaging 5.2%—our book-to-price ratio here remains healthy at 1.05x—and a 92% policy retention rate. New business submissions were up 14%, particularly in catastrophe-exposed coastal markets like Florida and California, where we've selectively expanded via our telematics-enhanced homeowners product, integrated with climate risk modeling from partners like RMS. We ceded just 18% to reinsurance, down from 22% last year, thanks to improved attritional loss picks. Personal Auto moderated to 4.6% growth after adjusting for the 2% volume dip from elevated bodily injury claims amid inflation-driven repair costs, with semiconductor shortages pushing parts pricing up 15% YoY. Our AI-driven pricing engine, powered by machine learning on 50 million+ miles of telematics data, helped achieve a 103% book-to-price and limit rate deviations to underperforming geographies.

Commercial Lines were up a robust 10.5% to $1.9 billion, or 40% of the mix. Commercial Property surged 13.2%, benefiting from the broader rate-on-rate environment where attached property renewals saw 8-10% hikes, akin to what we've seen at peers like Chubb and Travelers. Our focus on middle-market accounts—$5-50 million TIV—drove this, with new business up 18% as clients sought capacity amid reduced reinsurer appetites post-Irma-like events. Regionally, U.S. growth was 15%, Europe flat at 2% due to softening in the UK motor fleet book from regulatory pressures under the FCA's pricing remedies, and APAC accelerated to 22% via our Singapore hub targeting Australian wildfire exposures. We maintained ceded premiums at 25%, with favorable terms from our CatX program at Lloyd's.

Workers' Compensation delivered steady 8.3% growth to $650 million, supported by 6% payroll-compensated rate gains and a 95% retention in core states like Texas and New York. We've leaned into tech here with our ClaimsPredict platform, reducing large loss frequency by 12% through predictive analytics on return-to-work patterns—echoing initiatives at The Hartford. Medical trend inflation at 7.5% tempered upside, so we're piloting value-based provider networks to cap that at 5% next year.

Our high-margin Specialty Lines, now 18% of NWP at $1.25 billion, exploded 16.7%—the standout performer. Cyber led at 24.5% growth, capitalizing on the ransomware surge with premiums up amid attacks like the MOVEit breach; our standalone cyber product, with parametric triggers inspired by Corvus Group's model, captured 25% market share gain in E&S. Directors & Officers (D&O) grew 14.2%, riding SEC disclosure rules and M&A pickup, while Environmental Liability added 11% from ESG-driven demand in Europe under the Green Deal. APAC specialty was a bright spot at 28% growth, with expansions in parametric products for Southeast Asian typhoon risks.

This NWP profile reflects our 'Disciplined Growth 3.0' framework: exiting 5% of our legacy California wildfire book for better risk-adjusted returns, investing $150 million in digital underwriting platforms to boost submission-to-bind at 65%, and layering in alternative risk transfer like sidecars for our $2.5 billion cat tower at the January 1 renewals. Ex-weather, NWP grew 11.4%, outpacing the 6-7% industry average per AM Best data. Retention company-wide hit 93%, with organic growth at 7.2%. Looking ahead, we see sustained mid-teens specialty tailwinds, moderating personal lines pressure from softening auto rates, and commercial momentum if inflation eases. Our combined ratio of 92.1% supports reinvesting in growth while targeting 12-14% ROE.

Turning to loss ratio trends, a core metric underscoring our underwriting discipline. Excluding catastrophe losses, our full-year ex-cat loss ratio improved to 60.4%, down 210 basis points from 62.5% in 2022, reflecting proactive pricing, enhanced risk selection, and tech-driven initiatives. Including cats, it came in at 63.2%, a 260 bps improvement from 65.8% last year. Loss ratio is calculated as incurred losses and loss adjustment expenses divided by net earned premiums.

Claims frequency—measured as claims per exposure unit—declined across most lines. In Personal Auto, frequency fell 4.8% year-over-year to 7.2 claims per 100 vehicle years, aided by reduced miles driven amid high remote work persistence and our UnityDrive telematics program, now adopted by 28% of our policies—up from 18% in 2022. This mirrors industry trends at peers like Progressive and Geico, where usage-based insurance has shaved 3-5% off frequency. Commercial Auto was stronger, with a 6.2% drop to 5.9 claims per 100 vehicle years, benefiting from fleet telematics partnerships with clients like UPS and Sysco, integrating real-time dashcam data. Homeowners frequency held steady at 1.8 claims per 100 policies but improved ex-weather to 1.4, thanks to our HomeShield risk mitigation app encouraging smart leak detectors and storm shutters—uptake hit 15% in high-risk states.

Severity—the average payout per claim—rose 7.1% full-year to $4,820 per claim, fueled by inflation in repair costs, medical expenses, and litigation. Auto physical damage severity surged 9.2% to $5,100, driven by OEM parts shortages and labor rates climbing 12% amid technician shortages—echoed in Allstate's disclosures. Bodily injury severity rose 8.5% to $22,400, with rising nuclear verdicts in litigious states like Florida and California. Property severity increased 6.8% to $18,200 per claim, exacerbated by materials inflation like roofing up 11% and reinsurance friction post-Hurricane Ian. Commercial Lines saw milder 4.9% severity growth to $32,500, as our mid-market focus buffered against workers' comp medical trend, which eased to 5.2% from 7.1%.

Cats were a $285 million hit in Q4 alone—4.2 loss ratio points—from California wildfires and Midwest tornadoes, bringing full-year cat losses to 2.8 points versus 3.6 in 2022. Our robust reinsurance tower, with a $1.2 billion XS at 10% attachment and favorable ILW terms from Swiss Re, capped net exposure. Ex-cat, Personal Lines loss ratio was 59.8% (down 180 bps YoY), while Commercial hit 61.2% (down 240 bps).

Regionally, U.S. Northeast and Midwest (45% of premiums) had a stellar ex-cat loss ratio of 58.1%, with frequency down 5.5%. Southeast (30%) was pressured at 65.4% including 1.1 points of cats; Florida homeowners severity up 10%, prompting 12% average rate hikes. West Coast (20%) at 62.7%, with wildfire cats adding 0.8 points; California's Prop 103 constrained responses, but our FAIR Plan offload reduced exposure by 8%. International (5%, UK and Canada): 57.9%, bolstered by softer flood frequency and Canadian auto reforms.

Our $150 million tech investment in 2023—including Guidewire ClaimCenter upgrades and Einstein AI from Salesforce—accelerated cycle times by 22%, reducing loss adjustment expenses to 8.2% of premiums. In auto, machine learning flags 35% of high-severity claims pre-settlement. We're doubling down on underwriting discipline: portfolio optimization trimmed $450 million in underperforming risks, while expanding telematics and IoT bundles. Pricing actions totaled 9.2% across lines, with 95% book retention. We guide to a 61-63% full-year 2024 loss ratio, assuming normalized cats at 2.5 points, with severity moderating to +5% as inflation cools.

Before moving on, I'd like to provide color on changes in actuarial assumptions and their impact on reported earnings and the balance sheet. Actuarial assumptions are the cornerstone of our reserving and pricing across P&C, Life & Annuity, and Group Health segments, reflecting best estimates from emerging data, models, and macro trends. This quarter, we recorded a net favorable impact of $285 million after tax, contributing 15 basis points to our core ROE of 12.8%.

In Life & Annuity (42% of premiums), a $180 million favorable reserve release, or 8% of segment pre-tax income. Downward revision to base mortality rates by 2.5% across term life and UL blocks, informed by post-COVID normalization and SOA studies—U.S. rates spiked 15-20% in 2020-2021 but returned to pre-pandemic levels per CDC/SSA, with declines among 65-80 annuitants. Morbidity assumptions shaved 1.8% in LTC, with actual-to-expected ratio at 92% from 105%, via our Actuarial Modernization Initiative (AMI) integrating ML on telematics/wearables data, improving accuracy 22%. Discount rates up 45 bps to 4.2%, unlocking $95 million, benefiting fixed annuities (duration 7.2 years). U.S. captured 70%; UK under IFRS 17 boosted CSM by £42 million.

In P&C (35% of premiums), a $65 million headwind from CAT loss development and expense creep—strengthened ultimate reserves 3.2% on 2022 accident year for SCS severity, with 15% PML uplift per RMS v18.1 and NOAA data on 25% SCS frequency rise. Offset by 1.5% reduction in auto PD lapse rates via MyDrive (2.8M policyholders), improving lapse A/E to 95%. Europe Solvency II amplified €28 million on motor for EV battery risks.

Group Health and Specialty (23%): $120 million favorable from morbidity/utilization resets—disability income down 4.1% per LIMRA on hybrid work; stop-loss discount rates up 50 bps released $45 million. In Japan, longevity extended 0.4 years to 85.2 but offset by yen discount rates.

Netting it, 2.1 point loss ratio improvement to 61.8%, LAT margin to 18%, DAC amortization $72 million, EV up 5% to $28 billion, RBC to 520%. These updates reflect data-driven dynamic setting—AMI reduced volatility 30%. Ahead, neutral to $100-200 million favorable in 2025 from AI stochastic modeling, reinsurance clauses, regional tailwinds like Medicare, Solvency II, Asia bancassurance. Challenges: inflation at 3.2%, geopolitics; stress-testing +100 bps rates for $500 million release.

Our investment income for the quarter was $475 million, with yield reaching 4.25% annualized—up 55 bps YoY from 3.70% and 10 bps sequentially from Q2's 4.15%. Trailing twelve-month at 4.18%, above 3.75-4.00% target and peer 3.95% per AM Best. This contributed 28% of operating income, offsetting $320 million cats from Idalia/Maui analogs. Drivers: reinvestment at higher rates (10y Treasury 4.45%), repositioning, credit spreads. New money yield 5.10%.

Fixed maturities 72% ($32.4B), equities 12% ($5.4B, blue-chips), alternatives 10% ($4.5B, REITs/Blackstone), cash 6%. Taxable corporates (45%) at 4.85% (A-/BBB+, OAS 105 bps), munis 4.60% tax-equivalent, MBS/CMBS 4.75%. Equities 3.20% (overweight Chubb/Travelers), alternatives 6.80% (infrastructure). North America 85%, duration 5.2 years; Europe 8% green bonds; APAC 5%. ALM with Aladdin reduced DV01 15%; derisked HY; ESG 25% new FI. Guide Q4 4.30-4.40%, FY 4.22%.

With $258 billion invested assets—up 4% YoY—our allocation is 68% fixed income ($175B, duration 5.8 years matching liabilities 6.1, 92% IG A-/BBB+, yields 4.5% +150 bps over 10y Treasuries: 42% Treas/agencies, 28% IG corporates overweight financials, 18% structured incl Agency MBS/CLOs), 17% equities ($44B, beta 0.75: 25% financials, 20% healthcare, 15% tech; privates 15% KKR/Blackstone 12% IRR), 15% alternatives ($39B: real assets 40% RE/infra, priv credit 20%, hedge 10%; 7.1% YTD). De-risked equities to corporates; swaps $15B notional. Regional: NA 72% FI, Europe 18%, Asia 10%. Unrealized gains $4.1B. Balanced vs peers, raised FY guidance $10.8B up 6%.

We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with RBC ratio at 520%. Our expense ratio also improved to 24.5%.

For combined ratio guidance: Q4 94-97% full, 91-93% ex-cat (150 bps cats); FY2025 92.5-95.5% full, 90-92% ex-cat (2.5-3.5 pts cats), 50-100 bps better than FY2024's 95.8%. Loss ratio 66-68% ex-cat: rates +11% earned (auto 12.4%, comm auto 10.8%, HO 9.2%), non-renew $2.5B underperformers, telematics 45% (15% LR improvement), GLMs/GenAI shave 2 pts. Expense 24.5-25.5% via $180M synergies, RPA 15% claims automation. Portfolio shift to E&S/cyber; reinsurance stable ($4.5B QS, $1B cat bonds). Upside AI fraud 50 bps; risks inflation/regulatory.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial property and specialty lines. We are actively managing our exposure to severe convective storms and coastal wind risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-powered pricing engines like UnityPrice 2.0 and advanced catastrophe modeling with RMS v18.0, alongside selective non-renewals in high-exposure areas like Florida coastal and California wildfire zones to optimize our portfolio for risk-adjusted returns.

David Kim: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment, prioritizing ALM, RBC efficiency, and yield in a higher-for-longer rate world. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in investment-grade corporates, agency MBS, infrastructure alternatives, and quality equities, with strategic tilts toward ESG-aligned assets and private credit to capture illiquidity premiums while maintaining pristine credit quality and duration matching.

Jennifer Hayes: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including Guidewire upgrades, Einstein AI predictive analytics, ClaimsPredict for workers' comp, and RPA automation reducing cycle times 22% to 28 days. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times, flagged high-severity claims, and lower large loss frequency, all contributing to loss adjustment expenses at 8.2% and enhanced customer retention.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of pricing changes on premium volume?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, John. As Michael detailed, pricing was the bedrock, contributing 5.3 points to 8.2% GWP growth through disciplined hikes—9.2% auto, 11.5% homeowners, 8.7% commercial—offsetting elasticity while leveraging UnityDrive and UnityPrice 2.0 for precision. Retention at 87-95%, with Q4 moderating to 7-8%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated catastrophe activity on your business?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Emily. Cats totaled $1.2B YTD or 3.5 points, in line but up YoY from Helene/Milton analogs. Our tower—$1.2B XS, ILWs, $250M cat bonds—capped impact, with ex-cat CR 91.2%. Guidance embeds 150 bps Q4, 2.5-3.5 FY25, supported by non-renewals and PML uplifts.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes like California's Prop 103 and Florida reforms on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, David. Prop 103 scrutiny dipped CA submissions 4%, but telematics and FAIR Plan offloads reduced exposure 8%; Florida reforms delay litigation relief but prompted 12% hikes and 2.5% non-renewals capping wind at 15%. We're adapting via granular pricing and portfolio shifts to specialty/cyber for resilient growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel: Thanks. On loss ratio trends, how sustainable is the frequency improvement?

Jennifer Hayes: Frequency declines—4.8% auto, 6.2% comm auto—are durable from telematics (UnityDrive 42%, HomeShield 15%) and macro like remote work/mileage normalization. Severity +7.1% is the watch item, but pricing +9.2% and ML flagging offset; guide 61-63% FY24 ex-cat.

Operator: [Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session.]

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Unity Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
